title: Plan AT: AI Personal Finance
summary: Cash-flow review → budget → goals → investment plan → monthly review
scenario: For individuals and families tracking spending, budgeting and planning; AI assists with organizing and math — it is not investment advice and carries no decision responsibility.

steps.title: Review cash flow
steps.detail: Pull the last 3-6 months of income and expenses (bills, bank statements) into a spreadsheet and categorize by dining, housing, transport, entertainment and more. Have the model compute each category's share, monthly averages and anomalies to see where the money actually goes.
steps.tips: Aggregate three months first, then let the model categorize — steadier than guessing month by month; flag unclear charges as 'to verify'.

steps.title: Budget
steps.detail: Set a monthly budget across three buckets — essential / non-essential / savings & investments — and have the model set a reasonable cap per category against your history, with 10% headroom. Write it into a Notion tracking page.
steps.tips: Don't budget to zero flexibility; keep a 'free spend' allowance — consistency beats perfection.

steps.title: Goals
steps.detail: Define short-term (3-6 months emergency fund), mid-term (down payment, further study) and long-term (retirement) goals with amounts and deadlines. Have the model work backward to how much you must save each month and rank priorities.
steps.tips: Ask for the concrete number — 'save X per month to hit the goal in Y months' — that drives action better than a vague 'I'll save'.

steps.title: Investment plan
steps.detail: Based on risk tolerance and horizon, have the model compare common vehicles (deposits, money-market funds, index funds, bonds, stocks) in characteristics and use cases, and sketch an allocation direction. For specific products or trades, verify on official channels and consult a licensed advisor.
steps.tips: Ask the model to spell out 'what volatility this plan has and how much it can fall at worst'; if you can't stomach it, start with the conservative tier.

steps.title: Monthly review
steps.detail: At month-end, compare actuals to budget, have the model surface overspend and savings opportunities, update goal progress, and adjust next month's budget. Turn the review into a one-line action — halve takeout, switch to a cheaper plan.
steps.tips: Set a fixed monthly reminder; the quality of the review depends on the few entries you bother to record.

pitfalls.title: Treating AI as an investment advisor
pitfalls.detail: AI doesn't know your full financial picture or risk capacity and can't give compliant advice; for real investment decisions consult a licensed advisor and treat model output as reference only.

pitfalls.title: Budgeting too tightly to last
pitfalls.detail: A budget with zero slack collapses within a week or two; keep 10% headroom plus a free-spend allowance so it's sustainable.

pitfalls.title: Tracking without reviewing
pitfalls.detail: Three months of entries never reviewed equals no tracking; set a fixed monthly time to compare actuals against budget.

pitfalls.title: Exposing sensitive financial data
pitfalls.detail: Don't feed full account numbers or IDs to the model; use aggregated category totals and prefer privacy mode.
